analysis: Excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) are graded potentials that occur when a neurotransmitter binds to a receptor on the postsynaptic neuron, causing depolarization. Unlike action potentials, EPSPs are not all-or-nothing; they are graded and can vary in magnitude. EPSPs are depolarizing, not hyperpolarizing, and they can summate or be added together to reach the threshold for triggering an action potential. They do not spread long distances as they diminish with distance from the site of origin. EPSPs do not have a refractory period, which is a characteristic of action potentials.
